parts.label: Part 2
parts.title: Should top managers be promoted from within the company, or hired from outside?
parts.article:
Should top managers be promoted from within the company, or hired from outside

A The difference between companies is people. With capital and technology in plentiful supply, the critical resource for companies in the knowledge era will be human talent. Companies full of 'star' achievers will, by definition, outperform organisations without them. So firms should compete for the most talented people, attract them from other companies, pay them very well, and get rid of second-raters. This in essence has been the recruitment of the ambitious companies of the past decade, given definitive form by the consultancy McKinsey in the book The War for Talent. Although the intensity of the warfare subsequently subsided, it has been warming up again as the economy tightens: labour shortages, for example, are the reason that many governments are welcoming workers from abroad.

B The diagnosis — people are important — is so obvious it scarcely needs saying, but the apparently logical prescription — hire the best — is, like so much in management, profoundly wrong. The point was illuminated by the collapse of the major American company Enron, whose leaders, as a New Yorker article called 'The Talent Myth' related, were so convinced of their own cleverness that they believed that collective intelligence is the sum of a lot of individual intelligences. In fact, in a profound sense the two are opposites. Enron believed in stars, noted author Malcolm Gladwell, because they didn't believe in systems. But companies don't just create: 'they execute and compete and co-ordinate the efforts of many people, and the organisations that are most successful at that task are the ones where the system is the star'.

C The truth is that a company can't win the talent war by hiring stars — only lose it. New light is thrown on why this should be so by a study of the careers of 1,000 top analysts, published in the Harvard Business Review. The researchers found that when a company recruited a star performer, three things happened.

D First, star quality didn't easily transfer from one organisation to another. In many cases, when star performers switched employers, their performance dropped sharply and in some instances never recovered. Few people realise how much success is due to the working environment — systems, processes, leadership, accumulated embedded learning, which are absent in and can't be transported to the new firm. Moreover, precisely because of their past success, stars were unwilling to learn new tricks and antagonised those (on whom they now unknowingly depended) who could teach them. So they left, increasing their salary as they did so — a surprisingly high 36 per cent moved on within three years.

E Secondly, the performance of their new team suffered as a result of the tensions and resentment created by their arrival. Hiring a star has been compared to an organ transplant. The new organ can damage others by taking most of the blood supply, other organs can start aching or threaten to stop working, or the body can reject the transplant altogether.

F Thirdly, the share price fell, as investors sold stock, evidently to punish the company for its extravagance in spending money on the expensive new appointee. This is ironic, since the motive for importing stars was often to improve the share price.

G Everyone accepts the cliché that people make the organisation — but, in fact, to a far greater extent, the organisation makes the people. This is as true in the world of football as in business. Some football clubs buy very good — and very expensive — players, but the team may be less than the sum of its parts. Others put much more emphasis on developing systems: a setting within which less good players can improve, and which helps everyone to form an effective team. These clubs are often more successful than those with the stars. Similarly, a study of the performance of fund managers showed that just 30 per cent of variation in fund performance was due to the individual, compared to 70 per cent to the company-specific setting.

H That will be no surprise to those familiar with systems thinking. Deming, the management thinker, used to say that there was no point in criticising people when 90 per cent of performance variation was down to the system within which they worked. Consistent improvement, he said, is a matter not of raising the level of individual intelligence, but of the learning of the organisation as a whole.

I So if not by hiring stars, how can a company compete in the war for talent? It should grow its own. Some companies are not only better at creating stars, but also at retaining them. Because they have a much more sophisticated view of the interdependent relationship between star and system, they keep them longer without needing to pay exorbitant salaries. The star system is glamorous — for the few. But companies that use it rarely benefit to the extent that they expect. Bringing in high-paid talent from outside is rarely worthwhile, and the impact can be dire.

questions.question: an example of the importance of systems in a non-business context

analyses.content: G段拿足球俱乐部（非商业环境）打比方，说明建立好系统比单纯买大牌球星更重要。
你找具体公司名字时容易忽略题目要的是“非商业环境”，全篇只有G段的足球领域符合这一点。

Everyone accepts the cliché that people make the organisation — but, in fact, to a far greater extent, the organisation makes the people. This is as true in the world of football as in business. Some football clubs buy very good — and very expensive — players, but the team may be less than the sum of its parts. Others put much more emphasis on developing systems: a setting within which less good players can improve, and which helps everyone to form an effective team. These clubs are often more successful than those with the stars.

questions.question: advice on how businesses can acquire the best people

analyses.content: I段明确建议企业不该去外面挖人，而是要自己内部培养（grow its own）最优秀的人才。
你可能会被A段描述各公司疯狂抢人的现象误导，但那是客观现象，真正给出“建议”的只有最后一段。
So if not by hiring stars, how can a company compete in the war for talent? It should grow its own.

questions.question: a medical analogy to a star joining another company

analyses.content: E段直接把雇佣明星员工比作医学上的“器官移植（organ transplant）”，完美对应题目里的“医学比喻”。
看到“medical analogy”，你只需要回到原文寻找直接和医疗相关的词即可，不要强行联想其他段落里的水土不服。

Hiring a star has been compared to an organ transplant. The new organ can damage others by taking most of the blood supply, other organs can start aching or threaten to stop working, or the body can reject the transplant altogether.

questions.question: a claim that stars may not make necessary adaptations when they change companies

analyses.content: D段指出明星员工跳槽后“不愿意学习新把戏（unwilling to learn new tricks）”，正好对应题目说的没有做出必要的适应。
你可能在找改变公司的字眼，但要注意这道题的关键是找那些描述员工自己“拒绝改变和适应”的句子。

Few people realise how much success is due to the working environment — systems, processes, leadership, accumulated embedded learning, which are absent in and can't be transported to the new firm. Moreover, precisely because of their past success, stars were unwilling to learn new tricks and antagonised those (on whom they now unknowingly depended) who could teach them.

questions.question: an example of a company that suffered from a misplaced belief in the talents of its senior managers

analyses.content: B段举了安然公司（Enron）倒闭的例子，直接说明了他们因为盲目相信领导者的个人聪明才智而遭遇失败。
你可能会在全文寻找破产或失败的公司，但明确提到“因为迷信高管才能”而受损的具体公司只有B段的安然。

The point was illuminated by the collapse of the major American company Enron, whose leaders, as a New Yorker article called 'The Talent Myth' related, were so convinced of their own cleverness that they believed that collective intelligence is the sum of a lot of individual intelligences. In fact, in a profound sense the two are opposites. Enron believed in stars, noted author Malcolm Gladwell, because they didn't believe in systems.

groups.description: Write the correct letter, A-I, in boxes 14–18 on your answer sheet.

groups.contentHtml:
Research published in the Harvard Business Review
Research into the working lives of a large number of successful people working as revealed that hiring stars had three common effects. The stars often failed to maintain their performance, as much of their success came from the factors making up their old company’s . In fact, many of them soon left their new company to join another firm at a higher . Secondly, there was often a negative effect on co-workers in their at the new company. Thirdly, investors reduced their commitment to the company.

analyses.content: C段提到了一项关于1000名顶尖“分析师（analysts）”职业生涯的研究，题目问什么职业，直接填入即可。
题目问的是这群成功人士是作为什么身份在工作，你要紧盯数字“1,000 top”后面的职业名词，别填偏了。

New light is thrown on why this should be so by a study of the careers of 1,000 top analysts, published in the Harvard Business Review. The researchers found that when a company recruited a star performer, three things happened.
D段点出这些明星员工的成功很大程度上归功于原来公司的“工作环境（working environment）”。
原文破折号后面的systems、processes等都只是具体例子，你要填的是概括这些例子的总称“working environment”。
Few people realise how much success is due to the working environment — systems, processes, leadership, accumulated embedded learning, which are absent in and can't be transported to the new firm.
D段提到这些明星员工离开新公司跳槽时，提高了自己的“薪水（salary）”。
题目里的“at a higher...”就是原文“increasing their...”的同义替换，直接提取后面的名词salary就行。
So they left, increasing their salary as they did so — a surprisingly high 36 per cent moved on within three years.
E段开头直接说，因为他们的到来，他们所在“新团队（new team）”的绩效受到了负面影响。
原文说的是“performance of their new team suffered”，直接对应题目里的负面影响，千万别漏掉new只填team。
Secondly, the performance of their new team suffered as a result of the tensions and resentment created by their arrival.

groups.description:
Complete the summary below.
Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

questions.question: The War for Talent had a greater impact than its authors had expected.

analyses.content: A段虽然提到了《人才争夺战》这本书，但压根没说它造成的实际影响是不是超出了作者原本的预期。
你可能会自己脑补这本书既然这么出名那肯定影响很大，但判断题只能看原文有没有对比“预期”和“实际”，没提就是NOT GIVEN。

This in essence has been the recruitment of the ambitious companies of the past decade, given definitive form by the consultancy McKinsey in the book The War for Talent. Although the intensity of the warfare subsequently subsided, it has been warming up again as the economy tightens: labour shortages, for example, are the reason that many governments are welcoming workers from abroad.

questions.question: The economic situation of certain countries is leading to growing demand for foreign staff.

analyses.content: A段明确说经济收紧导致劳动力短缺，所以许多政府开始欢迎“来自国外的工人（workers from abroad）”，意思跟题目完全一致。
原文的“economy tightens”就是题目的“economic situation”，“welcoming workers from abroad”就是“demand for foreign staff”，完美对应，放心选YES。

Although the intensity of the warfare subsequently subsided, it has been warming up again as the economy tightens: labour shortages, for example, are the reason that many governments are welcoming workers from abroad.

questions.question: Enron failed through misfortune rather than poor management.

analyses.content: B段说安然倒闭是因为高管盲目迷信个人才智而不信系统，这是管理问题而不是题目说的“因为运气不好（misfortune）”。
你可能会把公司倒闭跟“不幸”画等号，但作者在这里明确点出倒闭的原因是高管糟糕的决策，并不是不可抗力的厄运。

The point was illuminated by the collapse of the major American company Enron, whose leaders, as a New Yorker article called 'The Talent Myth' related, were so convinced of their own cleverness that they believed that collective intelligence is the sum of a lot of individual intelligences. In fact, in a profound sense the two are opposites. Enron believed in stars, noted author Malcolm Gladwell, because they didn't believe in systems.

questions.question: Promoting internally is nearly always more effective than bringing in stars from outside.

analyses.content: I段总结说应该自己培养人才，从外面高薪挖人很少是值得的，完全同意题目说的内部晋升比外部挖人更有效。
你可能觉得题目里的“nearly always（几乎总是）”太绝对而不敢选，但原文最后用了“rarely worthwhile（极少值得）”和“dire（极糟的）”来全盘否定外部挖人，态度非常坚决。

So if not by hiring stars, how can a company compete in the war for talent? It should grow its own. Some companies are not only better at creating stars, but also at retaining them. Because they have a much more sophisticated view of the interdependent relationship between star and system, they keep them longer without needing to pay exorbitant salaries. The star system is glamorous — for the few. But companies that use it rarely benefit to the extent that they expect. Bringing in high-paid talent from outside is rarely worthwhile, and the impact can be dire.
